one_liner: Senior GS-15 analyst in USPTO's CFO office leading financial-management performance studies, data analytics, process governance and briefings for top leadership.
fit_summary: This GS-15 role requires one full year of GS-14-equivalent experience in financial-management decision support, large cross-functional project management, and data analytics briefing senior leaders. Daniel's known strengths are in politics, policy, relationships, and emergency-management consulting at IEM, and nothing on file shows senior-level financial-management or data-analytics work. Unless the IEM role involved leading budget, performance, or analytics work at a very senior level, Daniel likely won't meet the specialized experience bar.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens) and the fed-transition path, so no prior federal status is required.
One full year (52 weeks) of specialized experience equivalent to GS-14 in financial-management operational research/decision support, large-project management, and data management/analytics.
Education cannot substitute for experience at this grade.
Must pass the USA Hire assessment cut score across competencies like Reasoning, Decision Making, and Interpersonal Skills.
Clearance listed as 'Other' (likely a background investigation); on-site presence in Alexandria required with only 52 telework hours per year.
strategy: Before applying, honestly check your IEM work against each of the three specialized-experience paragraphs. If you can't point to a year of senior-level financial or analytics leadership, apply instead to GS-9 through GS-12 Management and Program Analyst roles, where your background fits better.

If you do apply, frame your IEM work in financial and performance terms. Examples include grant or disaster-recovery funding analysis, program performance metrics for government clients, and briefings to senior officials, but only if you actually did them.

Preview the questionnaire (link in the posting) and answer honestly. The posting warns that overstated answers can be rescored or disqualify you, and expert-level claims will be checked against your resume.
Keep the resume to two pages. For each job, list dates, hours per week, and duties phrased using the posting's specialized-experience language.
Prepare seriously for USA Hire, since falling below the cut score ends your candidacy. Mark the November 13, 2026 close date and submit several days early.
resume_bullets: Led [number]-person cross-functional team at IEM to [develop/improve] [process or plan] for [government client], applying project management principles to deliver [result] by [date].
Analyzed [dataset/program funding of $X] using [tools] and briefed [senior client officials] through issue papers and data visualizations, informing decisions on [topic].
Developed performance measures to evaluate program effectiveness for [disaster recovery/preparedness program], resulting in [outcome].
interview_questions: Describe a time you used data analysis to change a senior leader's decision on a financial or program issue.
How have you managed a large, cross-functional project to establish new policies or governance standards?
Walk us through how you would build an enterprise-wide process improvement program for financial management.
How do you tailor complex financial or analytical information for executive audiences?
watch_outs: The GS-15 specialized-experience bar is very high and education can't substitute, so Daniel is likely not to qualify.
The role is heavily on-site, with only 52 telework hours per year, which means commuting from Manassas to Alexandria.
USA Hire has a hard cut score, so failing or skipping it ends your consideration.
The posting is open only from October 30 to November 13, 2026, so you'll have just two weeks to apply.
